learningObjectives: Describe how Pega Platform localizes applications using Rulesets, language packs, and locale settings.
Identify design considerations for localization including picklist properties, dynamic values, Paragraph Rules, and Data Page controls.

elements.text: Localization in Pega is like preparing a restaurant menu for international guests: you translate the text (language), change the currency symbol and date formats (locale-specific components), and flip the layout for right-to-left readers (RTL). The language pack is a pre-translated menu template — it only works if it fits the same restaurant format (UI architecture) and edition (version).

elements.description: Adapts an application for a specific language or region by:
items: (2) converting locale-specific components (currency symbols, calendar settings)
(3) adapting the UI for right-to-left (RTL) text direction if relevant

elements.description: Pega first checks the browser locale. If the operator profile specifies a different locale, the profile locale takes precedence. If no Ruleset exists for the selected locale, the UI displays English (default).

A translated Ruleset with values for fields that typically appear in every application (button labels, prompts). Import via the Localization landing page. The pack must match the same version AND UI architecture (e.g., Constellation v8.8).

Create a package, translate it and import it on the App Studio Localization page. Depending on the content, translation uses JSON/Excel and packaged Paragraph HTML. GenAI-assisted text needs review. Test each target locale before relying on automatic Ruleset selection.

Change the current operator locale in Dev Studio and test the application. A fresh login may be needed. Review messages and correspondence as well as visible labels; correct missing translations and test again.
What can and cannot be localized in Constellation:
items: CAN localize: labels, captions, tooltips, instructions in Views and Portals
CANNOT localize: Decision tables and decision trees, Case Statuses, radio buttons and drop-down controls in a table

elements.description: App Studio and generated user Portals support localization. Dev Studio is not fully localized; untranslated developer content does not alone prove the user Portal translation failed.

elements.caption: Package creation, translation, import and locale testing. The Paragraph workflow uses ZIP; the topic also describes JSON/Excel text packages.

elements.description: When generating a translation package, Pega OMITS local properties with multiple values (e.g., picklist properties). You must add these manually by editing the localization file in Dev Studio.

elements.term: Dynamic values — must also be localized
elements.description: Translate the phrase around a dynamic placeholder, preserving its substitution purpose. The topic uses a pyMessages phrase with a user-name placeholder; changing the customer name itself is not phrase translation.

elements.term: Paragraph instructions — packaged HTML, manual translation
elements.description: Step-instruction Paragraph text is included in the ZIP as source HTML in paragraph/base. Translate the corresponding paragraph/translated HTML, upload the compressed package and test the target locale. Manual translation does not mean absence from the package.

For Data Page-backed radio/drop-down entries, add the missing values as separate rows in the Additional text localization record, then rebuild and import the package. If the Data Page is absent from Views, create its localization Rule manually. This is a package omission, not a blanket localization ban.

examPitfalls.title: Locale priority: operator profile overrides browser
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which locale setting takes precedence when an operator's profile locale conflicts with the browser locale. Candidates say 'browser' (it is the most visible setting to users). Operator profile locale overrides browser locale.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pega first checks browser locale, but if the operator profile specifies a different locale, the profile locale takes precedence.

examPitfalls.title: No matching locale Ruleset → English, not an error
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Without a locale Ruleset, the documented UI fallback is English. This does not establish that every possible translation or configuration failure is silent.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If the application does not contain a Ruleset for the selected locale, the UI displays the default language: English.

examPitfalls.title: Language pack must match both version AND UI architecture
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what must match when installing a language pack. Candidates check only the Pega version. A language pack must match BOTH the Platform version AND the UI architecture (Traditional vs Constellation) — a Constellation pack will not work on Traditional UI.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Language packs must match both the same version AND the same UI architecture. A Constellation v8.8 pack cannot be used in a Section-based v8.8 app.

examPitfalls.title: Picklist properties are omitted from translation packages
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what is included in a Pega translation package export. Candidates expect all text, including picklist options. Picklist property values are explicitly excluded from translation packages and must be translated separately.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Local multi-value properties need manual localization-file preparation in Dev Studio; do not generalize this omission to every possible picklist source.

examPitfalls.title: Paragraph Rules require manual translation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Manual translation and package exclusion are different. Step-instruction Paragraph source HTML is in the ZIP; its translated counterpart must be edited.
examPitfalls.bestPractice:
Paragraph Rules require manual translation. Edit the

tags in the paragraph/translated folder files within the translation ZIP package.

examPitfalls.title: Data Page controls not auto-included in translation package
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether Data Page control labels are captured by the translation package export. Candidates say yes. Data Page controls are not auto-included — they must be manually added to the translation scope.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Populate the associated Additional text localization record, rebuild and import. A Data Page absent from Views needs a manually created localization Rule.

examPitfalls.title: Cannot localize Decision tables, Case Statuses in Constellation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what content types can be localized in a Constellation application. Candidates include Decision Tables and Case Statuses. Both are explicitly unsupported for localization in Constellation — they cannot be translated.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In Constellation, you cannot localize: Decision tables and decision trees, Case Statuses, and radio buttons/drop-down controls in a table.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is beginning a project to extend a Pega Claims application to support French and German users in addition to English-speaking users. The project manager asks what localization in Pega Platform actually involves beyond simple text translation. What does localization in Pega Platform involve?

options.text: Translating text, converting locale-specific components (currency, calendars), and adapting the UI for RTL text if needed
Only translating the text in the application to the target language
Replacing all English text with translated text and redeploying the application
Configuring user roles to restrict access by region

practiceQuiz.hint: Localization covers more than language translation — it includes date, time, and currency formats.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Regional formatting and text direction matter alongside language.

optionExplanations.A: Regional formatting and text direction matter alongside language.
optionExplanations.B: Text alone leaves other locale needs unaddressed.
optionExplanations.C: Replacing English strings alone misses regional UI requirements.
optionExplanations.D: Access roles serve authorization rather than text localization.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The browser locale is French and the operator profile specifies German. A German locale Ruleset is available. Which setting takes precedence?

options.text: German — the operator profile locale overrides the browser locale
French — Pega always uses the browser locale
English — Pega defaults to English when there is a conflict
The user is prompted to choose between French and German

practiceQuiz.hint: When browser locale conflicts with operator profile locale, which one takes precedence in Pega?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The specified operator locale takes precedence over the browser.

optionExplanations.A: The specified operator locale takes precedence over the browser.
optionExplanations.B: Browser preference does not override this operator setting.
optionExplanations.C: Conflicting settings do not themselves force the English fallback.
optionExplanations.D: The source describes precedence rather than this automatic prompt.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user selects Japanese as their locale, but the application does not have a Japanese Ruleset. What does Pega display?

options.text: English — the default language
An error message indicating the locale is not supported
A blank application with no text
The application in the closest supported language

practiceQuiz.hint: Missing locale Rulesets fall back to the default.
practiceQuiz.rationale: English is the documented fallback for an absent locale Ruleset.

optionExplanations.A: English is the documented fallback for an absent locale Ruleset.
optionExplanations.B: An absent locale Ruleset does not imply this error outcome.
optionExplanations.C: The documented fallback keeps text visible in English.
optionExplanations.D: The topic specifies English, not nearest-language matching.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer tries to import a language pack into a Constellation v8.8 application, but the pack is for a Section-based v8.8 application. What happens?

options.text: The language pack is not supported — it must match the same UI architecture
The language pack works because it's the same Pega version
The language pack is automatically converted to Constellation format
The language pack works but only for button labels and prompts

practiceQuiz.hint: Both the version number AND the UI architecture must match when importing a language pack.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Matching release numbers alone does not satisfy UI compatibility.

optionExplanations.A: Matching release numbers alone does not satisfy UI compatibility.
optionExplanations.B: A matching release cannot compensate for a different architecture.
optionExplanations.C: The topic does not promise automatic architecture conversion.
optionExplanations.D: Partial label success is not the compatibility rule described.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After updating the operator record locale in Dev Studio, the developer does not see any UI language changes. What should they do?

options.text: Log out and log back into the application
Restart the Pega application server
Clear the translation package and re-import
Change the locale in Admin Studio instead of Dev Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: A simple session restart resolves locale refresh issues.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A fresh login can apply the operator locale change.

optionExplanations.A: A fresh login can apply the operator locale change.
optionExplanations.B: A server restart is not the routine locale verification step.
optionExplanations.C: Removing translation work is not needed for a session refresh.
optionExplanations.D: The topic uses the operator record in Dev Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following content types CANNOT be localized in a Constellation Pega application?

options.text: Decision tables and decision trees
Labels and captions in Views
Tooltips in Portals
Instructions in user-facing components

practiceQuiz.hint: One content type has an explicit Constellation localization limitation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The topic lists Decision tables and trees as unsupported.

optionExplanations.A: The topic lists Decision tables and trees as unsupported.
optionExplanations.B: View labels and captions are supported user-facing text.
optionExplanations.C: Portal tooltips are included among localizable UI text.
optionExplanations.D: User-facing instructions can be translated in supported contexts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following CANNOT be localized in Constellation applications? (Select 3)

options.text: Decision tables and decision trees
Case Statuses
Radio buttons and drop-down controls in a table
Labels and captions in Views

practiceQuiz.hint: Three of these are explicitly listed as Constellation localization limitations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Decision tables and trees are listed restrictions. Case Statuses are also listed as restrictions. The restriction specifically includes these controls inside tables.

optionExplanations.A: Decision tables and trees are listed restrictions.
optionExplanations.B: Case Statuses are also listed as restrictions.
optionExplanations.C: The restriction specifically includes these controls inside tables.
optionExplanations.D: View labels and captions are supported text rather than exclusions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Local multi-value property entries are absent from an auto-generated translation package. Which documented preparation step was missed?

options.text: Add the omitted local multi-value properties by editing their localization file in Dev Studio
Picklist properties require a separate Localization Ruleset to be created first
Picklist values are stored in Data Pages and must be translated in App Studio
The package was generated before the picklist Rule was saved

practiceQuiz.hint: Multi-value properties have special handling in translation packages.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented omission needs manual localization-file preparation.

optionExplanations.A: The documented omission needs manual localization-file preparation.
optionExplanations.B: A separate Ruleset prerequisite is not the omission described.
optionExplanations.C: Not every picklist is necessarily sourced from a Data Page.
optionExplanations.D: Saving the Rule alone does not address the documented omission.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer needs to localize step instructions stored in a Paragraph Rule. What is the correct approach?

options.text:
Edit the

tags in the paragraph/translated folder files within the translation ZIP, then upload and verify
Open the Paragraph Rule in App Studio and type the translated text directly
Use the Localization landing page to automatically translate Paragraph Rule text
Paragraph Rules cannot be localized in Pega Platform

practiceQuiz.hint: Paragraph Rules require manual editing in the translation package.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Edit the translated HTML and verify the imported Paragraph text.

optionExplanations.A: Edit the translated HTML and verify the imported Paragraph text.
optionExplanations.B: Overwriting the original Paragraph is not this packaged workflow.
optionExplanations.C: The Step-instruction workflow requires manual HTML translation.
optionExplanations.D: Paragraph text can be localized through the documented package.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Constellation application, drop-down controls are sourced from a Data Page. After generating a translation package, a developer notices these controls are not included. What should they do?

options.text: Add values in the associated Additional text localization record, then rebuild and import the package
Regenerate the translation package after populating the Data Page with test data
Convert the Data Page controls to hardcoded values before generating the package
Nothing — Data Page controls are automatically included after the first application run

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a dedicated place in App Studio Settings to add Data Page controls.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Prepare the associated localization record and rebuild the package.

optionExplanations.A: Prepare the associated localization record and rebuild the package.
optionExplanations.B: Runtime test data alone does not replace this localization step.
optionExplanations.C: Changing the control source does not perform its translation.
optionExplanations.D: The source requires preparation rather than automatic later inclusion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After all language Rulesets are imported and tested, how does Pega Platform determine which language to display for each user?

options.text: Use the matching locale Ruleset automatically after imports and locale testing
The developer must configure which language to display for each Access Group
Pega always displays the most recently imported language pack
The user selects their language on the login screen each session

practiceQuiz.hint: Once Rulesets are imported, Pega handles locale selection automatically.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Imported and tested translations are selected using the user locale.

optionExplanations.A: Imported and tested translations are selected using the user locale.
optionExplanations.B: Per-Access-Group language configuration is not the stated selection.
optionExplanations.C: Import order does not determine each user’s display locale.
optionExplanations.D: A repeated login-screen choice is not the mechanism described.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Constellation application uses a Data Page for a drop-down control, but the Data Page is not referenced in any View. How should the developer add it to the translation package?

options.text: Create the localization Rule for that Data Page manually
Reference the Data Page in at least one View, then regenerate the translation package
Add the Data Page values directly to the translation ZIP file using a text editor
It cannot be localized if not referenced in a View

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a manual fallback for unreferenced Data Pages.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create the localization Rule manually for this unreferenced page.

optionExplanations.A: Create the localization Rule manually for this unreferenced page.
optionExplanations.B: Adding a View reference is not the documented manual fallback.
optionExplanations.C: Direct ZIP edits are not the specified fallback for this case.
optionExplanations.D: Lack of a View reference does not prevent manual Rule creation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is implementing localization for a Pega application that must support English and Spanish users. Which TWO Pega components are used to implement language localization?

options.text: Language packs — pre-built Pega-provided translation bundles for UI labels, messages, and system-level portal text
Locale-specific Rulesets — containing localized versions of Paragraph rules, correspondence templates, and UI field labels for a target locale
Custom database tables created per language to store all translated field values outside of Pega Rulesets
Separate Pega application installations per language with no shared Rulesets between them

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega localizes via language packs (system text) and locale Rulesets (application-specific translated rules).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega packs provide common platform UI translations. Locale Rulesets hold the application-specific translated content.

optionExplanations.A: Pega packs provide common platform UI translations.
optionExplanations.B: Locale Rulesets hold the application-specific translated content.
optionExplanations.C: Separate external language tables are not required by this approach.
optionExplanations.D: Separate installations are not needed merely to support languages.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO preparation decisions match the documented localization design?

options.text: Translate reusable Step-instruction Paragraph HTML in the packaged translated folder
Manually prepare omitted local multi-value properties and Data Page-backed control entries
Create a separate Data Model per language to ensure field labels are stored in the correct locale
Standardize all date formats to US MM/DD/YYYY format to ensure data consistency across all locales

practiceQuiz.hint: Package omissions and manual translation require preparation; neither is solved by a separate language-specific data model.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Packaged Paragraph HTML allows translation of reusable instructions. Both omitted value sources require manual localization preparation.

optionExplanations.A: Packaged Paragraph HTML allows translation of reusable instructions.
optionExplanations.B: Both omitted value sources require manual localization preparation.
optionExplanations.C: Separate language data models are not required for translated display.
optionExplanations.D: Forcing US dates fails to respect other regional conventions.
